name: Riemann Hypothesis
question: Are all nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function on the line Re(s)=1/2?
first_attack: Audit precise statement and prove a restricted case
dispatch_next: Do not prioritize extending T = 36 inside the already-published critical-line verification range. First identify a mathematically new zero-free region, explicit bound, or verified statement not implied by existing computations.
dispatch_why: The new exact interval verifier reaches T = 36, but published computations cover zeta zeros vastly farther. Increasing a tiny certified height is not a new attack on the Riemann hypothesis.

campaign.method: Interval-arithmetic argument principle and Hardy Z sign changes
campaign.hypothesis: Every non-trivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part 1/2.
campaign.first_proof_obligation: A finite height is already classical. The next obligation is a zero-free statement with an explicit constant that does not follow from plugging this height into a known explicit formula, or a machine-checked count past the range a hand calculation can audit.
campaign.next_experiment: Raise the certified height by tightening the contour enclosures, then compare the isolating intervals against a published zero table entry by entry.
campaign.falsification: A height T at which the certified argument count N(T) strictly exceeds the number of disjoint intervals where Z changes sign.
campaign.blocker: T = 36 is far below Platt–Trudgian (at least 3*10^12). Extending the height needs a faster contour, not a new idea about the hypothesis.

probes.name: Riemann Hypothesis
probes.title: Critical-line zero count for zeta up to a small height
probes.frontier: Known: every non-trivial zero with imaginary part up to at least 3*10^12 lies on the critical line (Platt and Trudgian, and later computations go further). T <= 36 is classical. Reproduction only.

smoke.scope: Every non-trivial zero of zeta with imaginary part in (0, 23] is simple and lies on the critical line: the argument principle gives N(23) = 2, equal to the number of disjoint intervals where the Hardy Z-function changes sign.

deep.scope: Every non-trivial zero of zeta with imaginary part in (0, 36] is simple and lies on the critical line: the argument principle gives N(36) = 5, equal to the number of disjoint intervals where the Hardy Z-function changes sign.

probes.name: Riemann Hypothesis
probes.title: Certified zero count and critical-line location of every Riemann zero up to height T
probes.frontier: Known: every zero with 0 < Im s <= 3*10^12 is on the critical line and simple (Platt & Trudgian 2021); the first 10^13 zeros were located by Gourdon (2004). These heights reproduce classical computations (Gram, Backlund, Hutchinson).

smoke.scope: Exactly N(T) zeros of zeta(s) with 0 < Im s < T = 100 (counted with multiplicity, certified by the argument principle), and Z(t) has that many certified sign changes on (0, T]: all of them are simple zeros on Re s = 1/2.

deep.scope: Exactly N(T) zeros of zeta(s) with 0 < Im s < T = 1000 (counted with multiplicity, certified by the argument principle), and Z(t) has that many certified sign changes on (0, T]: all of them are simple zeros on Re s = 1/2.

milestones.title: The first two non-trivial zeta zeros are simple and on the critical line
milestones.scope: N(23) = 2, a classical height; not a proof of the Riemann hypothesis
milestones.description: Argument-principle count N(T) matched to Hardy Z sign changes on (14, 15) and (21, 22). The checker repeats the count with a different Euler-Maclaurin and Stirling truncation. The deep run reaches N(36) = 5.

milestones.title: All 29 Riemann zeros below height 100 certified simple and on the critical line
milestones.description: The argument principle certifies N(100) = 29 exactly from interval boxes along 2 -> 2+100i -> 1/2+100i, and Hardy's Z(t) has 29 certified sign changes on (0, 100]. All arithmetic is rigorous interval arithmetic with explicit series remainders, repeated by the checker at another precision and truncation. The deep run certifies all 649 zeros below height 1000 the same way.
